events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: American Icon The US Flag in Art
events.address: 4th and Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20565
events.description: Old Glory, reimagined: artists transform our flag over the centuries. Across generations, the Stars and Stripes has inspired pride, protest, and profound artistic expression. From battlefields to modern cultural movements, our flag's journey through art reveals a nation constantly redefining itself. This installation features some 30 artworks from the late 1800s to present day, tracing how the meaning of the US flag has evolved over time. It explores what the flag represents and how people connect with it. You’ll find paintings, prints, and photographs by renowned artists like Gordon Parks, Childe Hassam, Dorothea Lange, Jasper Johns, and Faith Ringgold.

events.title: Annapolis Witches & Legends Walking Tour
events.description: Take a walk through the history of Maryland's witch trials, superstition, and local legends with Annapolis Ghost Tours. Between the 1600s and 1700s, Maryland saw at least twelve witch trials. The last one was a capital case held right here in Annapolis. Several women in the colony were killed under suspicion of witchcraft, one was legally executed, and the stories of others have become legends that persist to this day. On this 90-minute walking tour, we will talk about the superstitions and accusations through the lens of local history.

The exhibition is part of a University of Maryland Arts for All-funded project aimed at engaging students in science communication through art, increasing awareness of insect biodiversity and ecological roles, fostering collaboration across disciplines, evaluating changes in attendee knowledge, attitudes, and intentions, and contributing to a replicable arts-based model for conservation education. The exhibition will highlight six Maryland insect species that are included on Maryland’s List of Rare, Threatened, and Endangered Animals . Original works created through the exhibition’s two different open calls will be displayed alongside science-based information about insect ecological roles, insect habitats, and key conservation actions. events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Explore the remarkable story of bison. These iconic animals shaped North American landscapes for more than 100,000 years and anchored Indigenous lifeways for generations. Pushed to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, bison survived thanks to dedicated conservation efforts. Today, they stand strong as an enduring symbol of survival and resilience. The Bison: Standing Strong exhibit invites you into this incredible journey. Explore a full-sized bull bison specimen, the six-foot-wide skull of an ancient bison ancestor, an immersive soundscape, multimedia, cutting-edge scientific research, and Native objects and stories shared in collaboration with community members. Experience the deep history of America’s national mammal and discover the hopeful future being built for generations to come.

Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students across four seminar courses conducted original research to deepen understanding of the collection and reconsider how these objects are interpreted and exhibited. events.description: More than 100 years ago, real bison grazed outside the Smithsonian Castle building. Bison are returning in a bold new way! Three larger-than-life bronze bison, created by sculptor Gary Staab, find a permanent home outside the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. These towering sculptures of a bull, cow, and calf are at 125 percent scale and modeled after taxidermy specimens seen at the Smithsonian between 1888 and 1957. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. Participants hear stories of where the old mills and roads were located and learn about famed military figures (particularly from the Civil War era) and colorful residents who graced the area. Numerous period photographs support the narrative, bringing history to life. Walking requirements are minimal, although one segment involves going down a slight grassy decline. The tour runs rain or shine. Snacks and water are included. Cost is $45 per seat. In the event of cancellation, refunds are provided if a replacement is found for the seat; a wait list is maintained for this purpose. There are 23 seats on the bus. Special "Event Pricing" is offered for the award-winning "Danger Between the Lines" DVD and tour-related illustrated books, available for purchase with cash only. Narrated Historic Bus Tour with Jim Lewis combines local history education, community connection, and immersive storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Questions? Email contact@greateroakton.com . events.title: Claiming the Sea: Asian Perspectives on Maritime Dominance
events.description: Asia’s seas have long served as arenas of commerce, cooperation, contestation, and conflict. Today, the maritime expanse stretching from the Indian Ocean to the Arctic stands at the center of global geopolitics, economic flows, environmental pressures, and strategic competition—military, legal, and otherwise. With these dynamics in mind, this conference seeks to foster interdisciplinary dialogue on how maritime dominance is conceptualized, pursued, and contested across Asian contexts. events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. Image: Boris Ignatovich (Russian, 1899-1976), Composer Dmitri Shostakovich, from "Ignatovich, Soviet Avant-Garde", 1928, gelatin silver print, 16 H x 20 W in. events.title: Emancipation Proclamation Rotunda Display
events.description: For the first time since 1952, the National Archives welcome new, permanent document cases in the Rotunda as it unveils the original 1863 Emancipation Proclamation signed by Abraham Lincoln. While the Founding Documents—the Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, and Bill of Rights—established the nation’s path during the revolutionary and colonial period, the addition of the Emancipation Proclamation to the Rotunda demonstrates the nation’s continued journey to expand rights to its citizens.

events.title: Entertainment Nation
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Entertainment has the power to captivate, inspire and transform us. It brings us together. We share it when we spontaneously recite lines from a favorite movie, dance to the same groove or recreate a national sports moment on a neighborhood street. It can also spur critical conversations, expose divides, and foster important historical change. Through the National Museum of American History’s extraordinary collection of theater, music, sports, movie and television objects, the exhibition features a powerful, ever-changing selection of objects and interactive experiences. Through the objects and their stories, the exhibition explores how, for more than 150 years, entertainment has provided a forum for important national conversations about who we are, and who we want to be.

events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.title: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn
events.description: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn explores the powerful history of Quaker families who came to Woodlawn to establish an antislavery community rooted in equality and nonviolence. Through innovative farming and free labor, they sought to demonstrate an alternative to slavery in Virginia, settling alongside a small, established free Black community already living in the area. This exhibit examines the parallel lives, shared aspirations, and evolving relationships between these neighboring communities. As part of the Virginia 250th commemoration, Friends Gather Here invites us to reflect on this quiet revolution and examine our nation’s foundational ideals. On View: June 27 – December 30, 2026 Admission: Free (with suggested donation)

events.description: Since their formation in 2014, HARBOUR has gone from packing rooms in their native Cincinnati to selling out venues across the United States. During their tenure as a group, HARBOUR has delivered 5 full length albums - the latest of which, entitled Great, Big, Insignificant, was released in October, 2025 after much anticipation. After supporting artists such as Bilmuri & Wilderado, HARBOUR successfully completed their first multinational headline tour in 2025. With more shows on the way in celebration of the new album, and even more music in the works, the band's future is sure to be anything but insignificant.

events.title: HU Dance Summit Series: Embodying a Continuum of Legacy
events.description: Join the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts at Howard University for the inaugural HU Dance Summit Series: Embodying a Continuum of Legacy, an evening celebrating the rich traditions, artistic innovation, and enduring influence of African Diasporic dance. Coinciding with the 33rd anniversary of the Howard University Dance Program, founded in 1993 under the visionary leadership of Dr. Sherrill Berryman Johnson, the Summit honors a legacy of artistic excellence while exploring the future of Black dance through dialogue, embodied learning, and interdisciplinary exchange. Inspired by the pioneering work of Katherine Dunham, the event features a scholar-and-artist conversation with distinguished panelists Denise Saunders Thompson, Michelle Gibson, and Akua Kouyaté-Tate, with opening remarks from Dean Raquel Monroe and panel moderation by Professor Gentry I. George. Attendees will also experience masterclasses in Afro Modern dance with Michelle N. Gibson and Dunham Technique with Sheila A. Ward, along with a special performance of Dr. Johnson's TESTIFY. Open to the Howard University community and the general public. Registration is required.

events.title: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

events.title: Is There Room for Revolutionary Conservatives in a Liberal Democracy? Lessons from the U.S. and Poland
events.description: In old and new democracies alike, the right has largely given up its traditional instinct to conserve. Instead, it has adopted the revolutionary tactics once associated with the Left. The United States (Donald Trump case) and Poland (Law & Justice—PiS case) are the two clearest cases in which this “conservative revolution” has gone full circle—seizing power, losing it, refusing to disappear, and then returning—all while holding on to somewhere between a third and a half of the electorate. The recent Oxford University Press volume Let’s Agree on Poland (eds. Maciej Kisilowski and Anna Wojciuk, 2025) confronts precisely the problems that follow from this situation, and forms the basis for this event. The event has four aims. The first is to introduce a U.S. policy, academic, and student audience to the “conservative revolutionaries” framework and to the Polish debate over a new social contract and the need for a new constitutional design. The second is to compare the Polish and American cycles of conservative revolution and liberal counter-revolution—the fights over courts, public media, the politics of prosecution, and contested transfers of power. The third is to ask whether institutional accommodation—federalism, decentralization, a vertical division of power—offers a realistic alternative to winner-takes-all politics in both countries. events.title: Join Historic Annapolis: Very Superstitious! Paca House and Garden Tour: A History of Luck, Lore, and Beliefs
events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. To see times, visit our October event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Weather or private events may alter the tour route. Please dress for the weather. Advance registration recommended; space is limited. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? Contact Cara Garside, Visitor Services Manager, at grouptours@annapolis.org . Accessibility Considerations : Accessing the interior of the William Paca House requires ascending and descending several flights of stairs. Photography Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to take photographs and video footage of people of all ages at Historic Annapolis-sponsored events for publicity. If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please opt out by notifying Historic Annapolis staff.

events.title: Legends & Lore
events.description: Come see the darker side of Frederick. When night falls, Frederick’s familiar streets have rather different stories to tell. Climb aboard our vintage double-decker for an hour of dark tales from Frederick’s past , researched from local histories, old accounts and the legends that have lingered long after the people involved have gone. As we make our way through the city, we’ll slow down at the very places connected to these stories, from historic streets and old buildings to some of Frederick’s more famously haunted places . Along the way, you’ll hear tales of strange happenings, restless spirits and the darker chapters of local history, all told against the backdrop of Frederick after dark. And because it’s October, you’ll also get a rather good view from the top deck as the city’s historic homes and neighborhoods put on their best autumn and Halloween displays. Whether you’re a believer, a skeptic, or simply enjoy a good story with a slightly unsettling ending, Legends and Lore offers a different way to discover Frederick’s history. Just remember, it’s much easier to laugh at a ghost story when you’re not sitting on the top deck in the dark. TOUR HIGHLIGHTS Hear researched tales of Frederick’s haunted places, local legends and darker history, told where the stories happened. Experience Frederick after dark from the top deck, with historic streets, autumn displays and a few places you’ll look at rather differently afterwards. TOUR DETAILS Price: $35 per person Duration: 1 hour Recommended Age: 14+ Departure: RAK Brewing Co, 400 Sagner Ave, Frederick, MD, 21701

events.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
events.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. Admission & Hours Free & open to the public Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open Friday, 12 to 7:30 p.m. Parking

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
events.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
events.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

events.title: The American Story
events.description: The National Archives Museum debuts a once-in-a generation redesign of its permanent exhibits: The American Story and the Discovery Center - connecting visitors with the National Archives in revolutionary ways. The American Story will showcase items and records in the National Archives that tell important moments in our nation's history. Visitors will get up close to more than 40 original artifacts and documents, including a rare 1823 Stone Engraving of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington's annotated copy of the Constitution, and presidential gifts including horseshoes to President Bush from Queen Elizabeth II. The American Story will be the first and only museum in Washington, DC to use artificial intelligence (AI) to bring each visitor a special, individualized opportunity to explore the records of the American people and engage with American history. This exhibit brings more than two million historic records to life, offering a personalized journey through our nation's past. This new museum experience provides all Americans with a special opportunity to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: We Make History
events.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

events.title: "MCP Servers Are a New Attack Surface: How to Securely Build and Use Them" at BSides Northern Virginia
events.venue: George Mason University Schar School of Policy and Government
events.description: Hear from GW Engineering alumnus Saquib Saifee, M.S. '23, Security Engineer at IBM, CISSP, eCPPT, at BSides Northern Virginia in Arlington, VA! On October 31, he will present "MCP Servers Are a New Attack Surface: How to Securely Build and Use Them" to an engaged audience of security engineers and AI practitioners. Model Context Protocol (MCP) is only as secure as the server you build it on. In under two years, it has become the standard integration layer connecting AI agents to enterprise systems, databases, source code, and production APIs. However, an agent crosses a trust boundary on every tool call and resource fetch, and the protocol leaves the server to decide what is allowed. If the server does not enforce those boundaries, nothing else will. Grounded in real-world incidents and contributions to the OWASP GenAI Security Project, this practitioner-focused talk provides an actionable builder’s guide to securing MCP architectures. events.title: A Dose of Dupas Presents: The Poetry Takeover Brunch
A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: Brady Art Gallery Tour: Unfossilizing African Art and Cracks & Reforms
events.description: Take a student-led tour of the exhibitions currently on view at the Brady Art Gallery: "Unfossilizing African Art" and "Cracks and Reforms". Unfossilizing African Art recontextualizes African material culture objects that have been held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students across four seminar courses conducted original research to deepen understanding of the collection and reconsider how these objects are interpreted and exhibited. Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection examines a decade shaped by political upheaval, social transformation, migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition. This exhibition, developed as part of an art history class taught by Associate Professor Bibi Obler, is accompanied by a catalog designed by graphic design students.

events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. Image: Boris Ignatovich (Russian, 1899-1976), Composer Dmitri Shostakovich, from "Ignatovich, Soviet Avant-Garde", 1928, gelatin silver print, 16 H x 20 W in. events.title: Echoes in the Gallery: Sharing Spirit Encounters & Spirit Inspired Poetry
events.description: An evening of intimate storytelling and remembrance. Share your personal encounters with spirits, your beloved departed, or the unseen. Or read poetry that bridges the living and the departed. It's not necessary to participate. We are happy to have your presence. Contact Kim to sign up or just show up. You're also welcome to visit the gallery anytime and add a photo/small offering of your departed relative or crossed-over pet to our community Ofrenda altar. It is currently set up in the gallery to celebrate Dia de Los Muertos and All Souls' Day, which starts on the eve of Oct. 31st. Dress is casual. The gallery will serve snacks, wine, and beverages. Those interested in sharing an encounter or poem are encouraged to contact Kim Yourick at kim@lockhousegallery.com or call 301-969-6676 to sign up. Our gallery hours are Thursday - Sat 10-7 and Sun 10-5 if you would like to come add to the Ofrenda. History of the Ofrenda (altar): An ofrenda (altar) during Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) is a sacred, temporary home or community table built to welcome and honor deceased family members and loved ones as their spirits return to visit the living on November 1 and 2. Rather than a place of mourning, the ofrenda is a joyful celebration of memory, identity, and continuing love. Key Elements of the Ofrenda and Their Meanings Every item placed on the ofrenda serves a specific purpose to guide, welcome, or honor the returning spirits: -Photographs & Personal Items: Pictures of the deceased go on the upper tiers so the spirit feels recognized, welcomed, and personally remembered. You may also include favorite toys, tools, or clothing. Marigolds ( Cempasúchil ): The bright orange and yellow "flower of the dead" has a strong fragrance and vibrant color believed to attract and guide souls from the spirit world back to the home. events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.title: Hitchcocktober at the Angelika
events.description: Join us this October to celebrate Alfred Hitchcock, the master who gave us some of the most suspenseful moments in film history! STRANGERS ON A TRAIN October 7 at 4:00 and 7:00 Guy Haines wants a divorce. Bruno Antony wants his father dead. When the two meet aboard a train, Bruno proposes a solution to both their problems: he will murder Guy’s wife and Guy will murder Bruno’s father, leaving two victims and no motives. REAR WINDOW October 14 at 4:00 and 7:00 A newspaper photographer (James Stewart) with a broken leg passes time by observing his neighbors through his window. One evening, he sees what he believes to be a murder and decides to solve the crime himself, with the help of his nurse and his girlfriend (Grace Kelly). SUSPICION October 21 at 4:00 and 7:00 After eloping with a charming playboy (Cary Grant), Lina McLaidlaw (Joan Fontaine) soon discovers his gambling vice and mounting debts. As his lies deepen and those around him meet mysterious ends, Lina begins to suspect that her husband’s affection may conceal a deadly motive— and that she could be his next victim. VERTIGO October 28 at 4:00 and 7:00 Retired San Francisco police detective Scottie Ferguson (James Stewart) wrestles with his personal demons as he finds himself becoming obsessed with the beautiful woman (Kim Novak) he has been hired to trail, whose husband believes she is possessed. PSYCHO October 31 at 4:00 and 7:00 When Marion Crane (Janet Leigh) ends up at the Bates Motel after making off with $40,000 cash, there's hardly a film fan alive who doesn't know what happens next. It wouldn't be Hitchcocktober without his biggest hit!

events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. events.title: Madds Buckley
events.description: In an increasingly artificial world, singer-songwriter Madds Buckley is staying undeniably human. An RIAA Gold-certified artist with more than 2 million monthly listeners, Buckley pairs clear vocals with unexpected melodies and a deep-rooted instinct for storytelling. Her music sits at a unique intersection: honest, accessible, and highly personal storytelling that often incorporates themes found in anime, video games, and narrative-driven media. Even at its most fantastical, her music never loses sight of what’s real. Following My Love Is Sick, Buckley continues to evolve with a new run of releases, including “Overboard,” “Concept Without Proof,” and “Human to You,” ahead of her forthcoming album Simple Binary and a Complex Phrase (out October 16). Expanding her sonic and thematic scope more than ever before, the album interrogates the artificial to get to the heart of what’s most real: loving, losing, and persevering through the pain. Madds Buckley has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 per ticket goes to supporting Conscious Alliance’s mission to end hunger nationwide and feed families in need.

events.description: Join us for our 2nd Annual Springsong Museum Meet & Greet, a free community celebration at the future home of Springsong Museum! 📍 Location: Burnt Mills East Park, 10701 Columbia Pike, Silver Spring, MD 20901 📅 Date: Saturday, October 31 🕙 Time: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM At Springsong Museum, fall is our time to mark milestones and show the community how much has happened in a year. Come explore the future site of the museum, meet the team, and learn more about what we’ve been doing. Leave inspired by Rachel Carson, the author and environmentalist whose sense of wonder and wisdom of nature are celebrated in Springsong. Carson lived most of her life in Silver Spring. Drop in and explore: Hands-on activities, including a nature observation station with microscopes Explore the architectural models and concept drawings for the new museum Learn more about Carson in her nature writings, early editions of her books, and magazine articles Observe nature up close on a native plant walk led by members of the Maryland Native Plant Society starting at 11am and 1pm For our Spring:Story Project , record what sparks wonder for you and your reflections on Carson in short interviews with a journalist Hear about the long history of the historic Burnt Mills site with a local architect Take a selfie with a life-sized cutout of Carson by the Northwest Branch Support the museum and help us spread the word by purchasing a Springsong tshirt !

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Ranger Tours at Peirce Mill
events.description: Step inside Peirce Mill, a rare surviving 19th-century gristmill in Rock Creek Park, and discover how waterpower once supported daily life in Washington, DC. Built in the 1820s, the mill served local farmers by grinding grain into flour and cornmeal. On this guided tour, you’ll explore the mill’s machinery, including the waterwheel, gears, and millstones that brought the process to life. Learn how the force of Rock Creek was harnessed to power the mill and the skill required to operate it. Rangers will share stories of the Peirce family and the workers who kept the mill running.

events.title: Ranger Tours at the Old Stone House
events.description: Step back in time with a ranger-led tour of the Old Stone House, the oldest building in the nation’s capital. Discover what life was like in the 18th century as you explore its simple rooms, learn about early residents, and uncover the stories hidden within its stone walls. Perfect for visitors of all ages, this short tour offers a glimpse into everyday colonial life right in the heart of the city.

events.title: Ratcliffe-Allison-Pozer House Tours

Tours are from 12 p.m. to 2 p.m. and there is public parking within 5 minutes.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musi

events.title: She Loves Me Musical on Halloween Night: Romance Instead of Haunted Houses
events.description: Not a Halloween Person? Spend Saturday night falling in love instead. Skip the haunted houses and fake cobwebs. This Saturday, October 31, The Little Theatre of Alexandria offers a different kind of night out: a lush, romantic musical set in a charming 1930s European perfumery. No scares, no costumes required, just heart, humor, and one of Broadway's most beloved scores. In a charming 1930s European perfumery, shop clerks Georg and Amalia can't stand each other. They bicker across the counter by day, never suspecting that each is the anonymous pen pal the other has been falling for by letter. As the holidays approach and the mystery unravels, two unlikely sweethearts discover that love may have been right in front of them all along. Set to a lush, witty score, it's the same timeless story that inspired the film You've Got Mail. Book by Joe Masteroff Music by Jerry Bock Lyrics by Sheldon Harnick Based on the play Parfumerie by Miklós László Directed and choreographed by Mitchell Aiello, with music direction by Isabel Hernandez-Cata. Produced by Eleanore Tapscott and assistant produced by Cassie Cope. Performances are Thursday through Saturday evenings at 8:00 PM and Sunday matinees at 2:00 PM at The Little Theatre of Alexandria, 600 Wolfe Street in Old Town Alexandria. Street parking. events.title: The Gathering Gloom: A Tribute to The Cure
events.address: 7750 Capital One Tower Road, Tysons, VA 22102
events.description: The Gathering Gloom is a passionate tribute to the timeless sound and dark romanticism of The Cure. Capturing the haunting atmosphere, shimmering guitar textures, and emotional depth that defined generations, The Gathering Gloom delivers an immersive live experience that honors the spirit and legacy of one of alternative music’s most iconic bands. From brooding early-era classics to sweeping anthems and pop-infused hits, The Gathering Gloom faithfully recreates the sound, look, and feeling of a true Cure concert. With meticulous attention to detail — from lush chorus-drenched guitars and melodic bass lines to dynamic stage presence — the band transports audiences back to the golden age of postpunk and gothic alternative. Whether performing beloved tracks like “Just Like Heaven,” “A Forest,” and “Lovesong,” or diving deep into fan-favorite cuts, The Gathering Gloom celebrates the music that defined moods, movements, and memories. For devoted Cure fans and newcomers alike, The Gathering Gloom isn’t just a tribute — it’s an experience steeped in atmosphere, nostalgia, and pure sonic devotion. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

events.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show - Halloween Spectacular with Live Shadow Cast!
The Speaks & Crash Boom Bang with Kill for Sushi
events.description: Three DC-area acts take the stage for an evening of pop-rock energy and local legacy. The Speaks, active from 1997 to 2009, broke down barriers with anthemic music and legendary live shows, earning radio play on DC101 and selling out five consecutive 9:30 Club shows. Signed to Warner Music (Asia) in 2005, their single "High" received unprecedented worldwide airplay and remains covered by artists globally; still streamed over 1 million times monthly. Crash Boom Bang returns to the stage in 2026 after a decade away, reuniting the band that helped define DC's pop-rock chapter. They cut their teeth at Jammin' Java, packing the house show after show before touring alongside Plain White T's, Mayday Parade, and Gin Blossoms. Their 2012 EP These Wild Things earned film and TV placements, while their "V.I.P." music video surpassed 300,000 views. Produced by Tom Higgenson of Plain White T's, their debut Gold Rush set the tone for their signature anthemic hooks and high-energy sound. Now they return home for one night only. Kill For Sushi, the rebranded project of Angie Pepa and former Wandering Lies bandmates, brings a new musical direction. As Wandering Lies, they won four battle-of-the-bands competitions and earned 2021 WAMA nominations. Their new album arrives in 2026. Jammin' Java celebrates these hometown forces in Fairfax County, Virginia.

events.title: The Speaks + Crash Boom Bang: Spooky Halloween Party!
events.description: From 1997 to 2009, The Speaks were known for 3 things: great anthemic music, amazing live shows, and drinking copious amounts of alcohol. From their radio debut on DC101 in 2003 to their 5th sell out show at the 9:30 club for their finale, The Speaks, who's members are of Filipino heritage, broke down barriers and were able to reach fans from all over the globe. In 2005, The Speaks signed a deal with Warner Music (Asia) with the "Life's a Joke" album release in the Philippines. The second single of the album, "High" received an unprecedented amount of worldwide airplay and is still being covered today from artists all over the world on YouTube. The Speaks released their final EP, "This is the Time" in 2008 and was distributed by Universal Music (Asia). From sharing the stage with national acts, to having their music videos receive heavy rotation on MTV Asia and MYX Music Channel, and still to this day being streamed over 1 million times monthly, The Speaks left their mark on the music scene and plenty of hangovers all over the world. Crash Boom Bang returns to the stage in 2026 after nearly a decade away, reuniting the band that helped define a chapter of the Washington DC pop-rock

events.description: Mount Vernon transforms into a spooktacular Halloween celebration with trick-or-treating fun and enchanting 18th-century entertainment on Thursday, October 31st, 2026 from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. in Fairfax County, Virginia. Young ghouls and goblins collect candy in a special Mount Vernon treat bag around the historic grounds—a Halloween adventure like no other! The sweet haul includes a variety of treats (while supplies last). Costumed children strut their stuff in a delightful costume parade through the historic area at 4:00 p.m., perfect for capturing Instagram-worthy memories. Step back in time with fascinating colonial demonstrations: watch sparks ignite at the Blacksmith Shop, discover how textiles were hand-woven at the Spinning House, grab fresh-baked bread from Justin Cherry's 18th-century bake oven demonstration on the 12-acre field, and witness the traditional magic of apple butter-making. Meet Mount Vernon's livestock, enjoy a pumpkin discovery station and straw bale selfie station, and experience enchanting 18th-century magic with Mr. Peter Gardiner (3:00–3:30 p.m. and 4:30–5:00 p.m.) on the Bowling Green. Hear Musical Stories with Robert Mouland (3:00–3:30 p.m.) and Music of the Revolution (2:30–3:00 p.m.). Meet General George Washington and Lady Martha Washington throughout the historic areas. After trick-or-treating, kids ages 12 and under dine free from the kids' menu at Mount Vernon Inn Restaurant from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. (one free kid's meal per adult entree; dine-in only). Admission: ages 12+ $31 general public/$24.80 members; ages 11 and under $26 general public/$20.80 members. Adults not collecting candy: $30 general public/free for members (registration required). Dogs are not allowed. All members must have either a trick-or-treating ticket or register to attend. Event runs rain or shine. Halloween at Mount Vernon combines trick-or-treating thrills with authentic colonial experiences and family dining in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover Mo

events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: Vintage China Cake Stand Workshop
events.description: Downtown Leesburg’s Most Nostalgic Creative Experience Step inside a beautifully restored historic building in the heart of downtown Leesburg and take part in a hands-on workshop that turns timeless china into a memory you can take home. The Vintage China Workshop at The Global Local invites guests to slow down, get creative, and give new life to carefully curated vintage pieces. Guests choose from an ever-changing selection of vintage plates and components, which are drilled on-site before being assembled into a custom tiered stand or serving piece. Each finished creation becomes a one-of-a-kind keepsake, perfect for celebrating a special day, gathering with friends, or marking a meaningful moment spent exploring historic Leesburg. The workshop itself is complimentary, with each stand individually priced based on the vintage pieces you choose to build. Our team handles all technical preparation and guides you through assembly, making the experience easy and approachable for all skill levels. Vintage China Workshops are held Saturdays and Sundays from 12–4 PM. Each guest receives a 10% in-store shopping discount on the day of their workshop. Please visit our website for current details and availability. Reservations are recommended. Walk-ins are welcome if space allows.

events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: A Quiet Space: Silent Retreat Near Annapolis, MD
events.description: A Quiet Space A Silent Retreat for Rest, Reflection & Renewal Before the gatherings. Before the shopping. Before the travel. Before the expectations. Before the season asks you to give so much of yourself, give yourself a place to pause. A Quiet Space is a gentle, intentionally designed silent retreat at Harmony Hills in Deale, Maryland, created for rest, reflection, and renewal. For a few hours, step away from the noise and demands of everyday life and enter a quieter space—one where you don't have to perform, produce, solve, or explain. Simply be. Through intentional silence, reflection, stillness, and spaciousness, you'll have an opportunity to reconnect with yourself and notice what may be asking for your attention. You don't need to arrive with a particular intention. You don't need to know what you need. You don't need to have anything figured out. Just come as you are. Whether you're moving through a season of change, carrying something unseen, feeling the weight of the upcoming holidays, or simply longing for a little more quiet in your life, there is room for you here. A Quiet Space includes: • Guided moments of reflection • Periods of intentional silence • Time for personal rest and stillness • Gentle grounding practices • Space to journal, reflect, or simply be • A peaceful setting at Harmony Hills Choose the amount of quiet that feels right for you. This experience is designed with different retreat lengths so you can choose the amount of time that best meets you where you are.

events.title: African American Quilt Documentation Day in DC
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts - Great Hall
events.address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005-3970
events.description: WASHINGTON, DC — The African American Quilt Documentation Study Group (AAQDSG) will host a FREE quilt documentation event in Washington, DC on Sunday, November 1, 2026, inviting the African American community to bring family quilts in to be documented, preserved, and honored as part of our shared history. Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Location: National Museum of Women in the Arts, 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005 Cost: Free — pre-registration required (time slots are limited) Since the 1980s, quilt documentation has been used to preserve family legacies and record the social, cultural, and artistic significance of quilts. African American family quilts have historically been excluded from this process. Most exist today with no documented history of the quilt or its maker — what's known has been passed down orally and never recorded. "Documentation is how we hold onto that," said A'donna Richardson, Director of AAQDSG. "It's an act of honoring our ancestors, of making sure the work of the quilt maker's hands is remembered. It's a way of saying: our ancestors mattered, what they made matters, and the stories tied to their quilts matter." The process reaches beyond individual families. Documented quilts become part of the historical record that scholars, museums, and researchers rely on to understand African American creativity, survival, faith, and community. Without this work, those stories remain untold and the historical record remains misrepresented and incomplete. We are encouraging the African American community to bring their family quilts, in whatever condition (the older, the better), to the November 1 event to have them photographed and documented, and to share the stories behind them. YOU MUST REGISTER to attend: https://aaqdsg.org/events If all appointment slots are filled, send your name and contact information to afamquilydoc@aadqsg.org. Contact: A'donna Richardson, Director, AAQDSG Website: https://aaqdsg.org Email:

events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Corey Arceneaux & the Zydeco Hot Peppers
events.description: 6:00pm • $20 • Tickets on Eventbrite and at the door if available Corey Arceneaux and the Zydeco Hot Peppers Corey Arceneaux and the Zydeco Hot Peppers bring the heat of Southwest Louisiana straight to the DMV with an electrifying mix of authentic zydeco, Creole rhythms, and dance-floor energy. A Louisiana native, Corey Arceneaux is a powerhouse accordionist and bandleader whose sound is rooted in tradition and shaped by legends like Clifton Chenier and Buckwheat Zydeco—who also served as a mentor and friend. With five studio albums and decades of international touring, Corey delivers a show that’s as genuine as it is high-energy. Now based in Virginia, Corey has assembled a seasoned all-star lineup of regional players who live and breathe roots music. The Zydeco Hot Peppers feature Ben Holmes (drums), a veteran of global zydeco tours and DC favorites; Doug Bell (guitar), a staple of the East Coast roots scene; Gene Monroe (bass), whose credits span blues, rock, and beyond; and Pat Clark (frottoir), a multi-instrumentalist with deep ties to New Orleans traditions. Together, they create a groove that’s equal parts bayou party and dancehall throwdown. Whether it’s a festival stage, club night, or Mardi Gras celebration, Corey Arceneaux and the Zydeco Hot Peppers turn every performance into a full-on Louisiana experience—accordion-driven, rhythm-heavy, and impossible to sit still for. events.description: Join The Radical for a celebration of Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead), a Mexican tradition that brings family, friends, and communities together to remember and honor loved ones who have passed, while celebrating the joy of life and the memories that keep their spirits alive. We're bringing together craft cocktails, delicious Mexican food from La Carreta Tortas y Tacos, music, and family-friendly activities for an afternoon and evening of food, drink, remembrance, and community. What to expect: Craft cocktails from The Radical, including special Día de Muertos-inspired offerings alongside our regular favorites. Authentic Mexican food from La Carreta, serving up delicious food to enjoy throughout the celebration. Music and a festive atmosphere to bring people together throughout the day and evening. Family-friendly themed activities inspired by the colors, creativity, and traditions of Día de Muertos. A chance to gather and remember, celebrating the people, stories, and connections that remain with us. Whether you're familiar with Día de Muertos traditions or discovering them for the first time, we invite you to join us in celebrating the rich cultural heritage behind this occasion and the universal importance of remembering those who came before us. Bring your friends, bring your family, and come spend some time with your neighbors as we celebrate life, memory, and community in the heart of Brunswick.

This Takoma Park self-defense class focuses on realistic adult training rather than sport, competition, or memorized routines. Participants will receive an introduction to Maryland Systema’s approach to self-protection through breathing, relaxation, posture, structure, and natural movement. The class includes instructor-led exercises and controlled contact. Training begins gradually so participants can learn how balance, distance, positioning, and decision-making affect personal safety. No previous martial arts or self-defense experience is required. The class is designed for adult beginners and people who may feel unsure about joining a traditional martial arts school. events.description: October 9, 2026 – November 1, 2026 Gallery Hours: Friday-Saturday, 12-5pm; Sunday, 11am-2pm Opening Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-8pm Layered Lives: Women in Print brings together women artists from the DMV region who explore the depths of lived experience through experimental printmaking techniques. events.title: Ghost Doctors Hunting Tour-Manassas Virginia...Experience The Paranormal!
events.description: Experience a Halloween ghost hunt one more time...and the ghost are still sticking around! Embark on a supernatural adventure in Old Town Manassas Virginia! Join us for a truly immersive and spine-chilling experience in Historic Old Town Manassas. Prepare to be amazed as you delve into the world of paranormal activity that has inhabited this town for over 150 years. Brace yourself for the unexpected, as you never know who or what might make an appearance! As seen on network and cable television from coast to coast paranormal investigators and tour guides to the supernatural, the Ghost Doctors, will lead you through the darkened streets passing century old buildings on a supernatural trek in Historic Old Town Manassas. This is not your typical ghost tour where stories are told; this is an authentic ghost hunt. Step into the shoes of a paranormal investigator as the Ghost Doctors will instruct you with hands-on experience with real ghost hunting equipment as you learn the protocols of the trade. Immerse yourself in the history of this remarkable city nestled in the heart of Northern Virginia, while you search for the lingering spirits of the Civil War era. For an unforgettable paranormal adventure Who ya gonna call? ... Ghost Doctors! For tour and ticket info including future tour dates visit: https://ghostdoctors.com or call (703) 686-4564.

events.title: Halloween Costume Mural Tour of Southwest DC, Navy Yard, and Capitol Hill! – eWheel Going Out Group
events.description: RSVP here... luma.com/tldgl9z7 -- Let’s get together for our final tour of the year! Put on your best Halloween costume and join us for an epic day in DC (dress code includes costumes, did I mention costumes, just to be clear costumes)! Fun fact: Washington, DC is home to roughly 150 murals, 500 outdoor sculptures, and 75 historic landmarks… and we’re going to explore a bunch of them! Come join us for a fun, free ~6.6-mile e-wheel adventure through Southwest DC, Navy Yard, and Capitol Hill, where we’ll discover incredible murals, fascinating memorials, historic landmarks, and some of the coolest sights hiding in plain sight around the city. Along the way, we’ll make numerous stops for photos, sightseeing, neighborhood exploration, and catching up with the group. I’ll also read aloud a short description of each mural, memorial, and landmark so everyone can learn the stories behind the places we’re seeing. You may be surprised by just how many amazing treasures are right here in our own backyard!

events.description: St. Anne’s Episcopal Church’s Fall Adult Forum: Church and State takes a look at military chaplaincy at 11:30 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1, at the church’s Parish Hall, 199 Duke of Gloucester St ., Annapolis, Md. The Rt. Rev. Ann Ritonia, bishop suffragan for the Armed Forces & Federal Ministries of the Episcopal Church, will speak at the forum. Her topic is “Theology of Military Chaplaincy: Spiritual Care & Leadereship in War and Peace.” Ritonia has a musical and military background. She studied music at the New England Conservatory of Music, playing the euphonium, and later attended the Armed Forces School of Music. She graduated from the U.S. Marine Corps Officer Candidates School and served 17 years in the Marine Corps and Marine Corps Reserve, holding a variety of leadership positions and attaining the rank of major before her retirement. Before her episcopal appointment, Ritonia served in parishes in Virginia, Connecticut and Maryland. She was also chaplain to the Marine Corps League and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs healthcare system. In her new role as bishop suffragan, she oversees and supports more than 100 Episcopal chaplains. The public is invited to attend this forum, and the next forum which will be held at 11:30 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 8, at the Parish Hall. On Nov. 8, J. Ernest Green, St. Anne’s music director, and Larry Molinaro, the church’s associate music director, will talk about “Sacred Music in Church & State.”

Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.
