events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Saint Cecelia Harvest Wine Dinner and Ball
events.description: In the years before a national Thanksgiving Day friends and neighbors would gather for a harvest dinner, giving thanks for the blessings of the year and for the promise of the dawning of the next. These dinners always included social dancing such as the Virginia Reel. Because these celebrations occurred in November they became associated with Saint Cecelia, who in some liturgical calendars was identified as the patron of music. At Shiloh Manor Farm we continue this old Virginia tradition! We are partnering with Magnolias at the Mill to present a tradition Saint Cecelia dinner inspired by a 200 year old book on Virginia cooking authored by one of Patrick Henry’s granddaughters. Following dinner musicians from the Greater Washington Folklore Society will perform traditional English Country Dance tunes that were well known in colonial Virginia such as the Virginia Reel. Dan Gillespie, a highly respected historical dance master will be on hand to teach and call the dances. No experience needed! Comfortable clothing and shoes are a must but we encourage formal or historic attire. A prize will be awarded for best costume!

events.title: Sourdough Bread Baking Class
events.venue: Kitchen at Grace United Church of Christ
events.description: Join Frederick home bakers Jon & Emily for a sourdough bread baking class designed for beginner bakers! Slow-fermented sourdough bread is beloved for its digestibility (especially for those of us with gluten sensitivity), lower glycemic index, and its keeping power without preservatives. Its complex, delicious flavor and airy, chewy texture cannot be beat! Beyond the joys of eating sourdough bread, many also enjoy the therapeutic nature of a slow, mindful hobby that doubles as a satisfying creative outlet. It's a science experiment you get to eat! In this 2-hour class, we will practice mixing, shaping, and baking a traditional sourdough bâtard (an oval-shaped loaf). You will leave class with: • your own sourdough starter (+ feeding instructions) • banneton proofing basket + cloth liner + bench scraper • a shaped dough to bake at home the same afternoon as class • a bonus dough to practice another shape & bake at home • printed and PDF versions of the recipe and instructions taught in class • support from your new sourdough bread baking friends!

events.description: Do you find that print is getting smaller so that you struggle to get the information? Do you have a condition that makes it challenging to read, write and spell? Did you know as of November 24 th , 2026, all Maryland pharmacies must provide accessible bag tags, prescription labels and medical guides at no additional cost to the individual and in a timeframe similar to other customers who use these services? events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare. This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps! We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls. Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside? Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation? Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure. Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by. End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book. Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.
events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour

events.venue: Ride the River with Anacostia Riverkeeper
events.description: Join us in the fight for a healthy, swimmable, fishable Anacostia River!Location: Atlas Brew Works Bridge District, immediately across from the Frederick Douglass Bridge in Anacostia. It offers easy access to the Anacostia River Trail and is the perfect spot for the post-ride festival.Route: Atlas Bridge District to Bladensburg Waterfront Park and back, a roughly 16-mile ride that covers the main stem of the Anacostia River. Turnaround points are included for those who need a shorter route.At Anacostia Riverkeeper, we are dedicated to protecting the Anacostia River for all who live, work, and play in its watershed. We create meaningful encounters with the river for all people in order to open opportunities for enjoyment of the Anacostia River. As an organization, our primary programmatic goals that help us achieve our mission are centered on trash mitigation, advocacy, water quality, stormwater reduction, and river access. All these programs have a strong community component, whether it’s having local volunteers collect water quality samples or taking a school group out on a free educational boat tour.Through a combination of outreach, advocacy, and science-based research our programs work to protect the water and the ecosystems it supports as well as foster deeper watershed appreciation through community connections and opportunities. The Anacostia community has long been neglected both environmentally and socioeconomically, with a legacy of industry and environmental racism forming much of the historical foundation surrounding the river. However, with the help of Anacostia Riverkeeper and other local grassroots organizations, progress has been made to make the river not only safer but more accessible and approachable for the people who live along its banks.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare. This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps! We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls. Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside? Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation? Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure. Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by. End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book. Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.
events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour

events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcomed but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). Please arrive early to ensure a timely start. Duration: Approximately 90 minutes. Fall Schedule & Locations Sunday, October 11 | Woodlawn Sunday, October 25 | Pope-Leighey House Sunday, November 1 | Woodlawn Sunday, November 8 | Pope-Leighey House Tickets & Policies Price: $30 per ticket. All purchases directly support the preservation of this historic site. Weather: Programs take place rain or shine.

events.description: Fathom Gallery Prospect Street (3251 Prospect Street NW, Suite 275) opens its doors on Wednesday, November 4 from 5PM to 7PM for an exhibit open house featuring Gathering Light, the first solo show by California artist Jennifer Magee. Guests are invited to enjoy light bites from Plan It to the T catering and bubbly while exploring the exhibit. Here, in Jennifer’s own words, is what inspired Gathering Light: “I have spent decades paying attention to the ordinary: a familiar path, a corner of the garden, the hour when light lands on a surface and stays just long enough to be noticed. My work is an argument for staying. In paint, cyanotype, and mixed media, I capture what daily attention gives back, with feeling always coming first. Gathering Light grew from my garden, my daily walks, and hikes across the desert Southwest, and invites you to wander, linger, and look closely.” (Photo courtesy of Fathom Gallery)

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

As you walk through the wooded landscape of Rock Creek Park, you’ll uncover how this fort helped protect the nation’s capital during a time of conflict. events.description: Do you want to connect with nature but you’re not sure how to get started? Do you want to be more present outside and escape the distractions of the modern era? Take a junior naturalist hike with a ranger and learn how to observe and study the natural world around you as you hike between ½ - 1 ½ miles through the Rock Creek Valley. Come prepared with water, appropriate layers, comfortable hiking shoes, and an open mind willing to practice a new skill. Recommended ages 8+. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm. Be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.
